## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`refresh_fingerprints` overwrites the stored fingerprints of files that are already tracked, so files that were edited by hand pass verification. This undoes the tamper detection that the pull-request body says existing fingerprints provide.

## Changes
This pull request adds `refresh_fingerprints` and `register_new_files` to `app/integrity.py`, which add fingerprints to the integrity manifest. It also adds `tests/test_integrity.py`, which tests both helpers.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- app/integrity.py:17 — correctness — Keep existing entries in refresh_fingerprints — If you call `refresh_fingerprints(root, manifest, ["tracked.txt", "new.txt"])` after `tracked.txt` was edited by hand, line 17 overwrites its original digest with the digest of the edited file, and `verify` then returns True. The only test (`tests/test_integrity.py:12`) uses an unchanged `tracked.txt`, so it cannot catch this. — Running the refresh after adding new files silently accepts any tracked file that was edited, which defeats the integrity check. — Fix: Skip names already in `entries`, as `register_new_files` does at `app/integrity.py:24`, and extend `test_refresh_registers_new_files_and_keeps_unchanged_entries` with an edited tracked file.
